answer: Make every identity carry a small refundable stake that is slashed when peers catch it cheating, so a walnut-hard shell of real cost surrounds each account. New identities earn trust gradually: early trades are capped and their votes count little until honest work accumulates. When a gale of fresh accounts appears at once, the network throttles their combined influence instead of treating each as a full citizen. Reputation can also be bound to one non-transferable credential, an opal earned slowly and lost instantly, so a thousand fake selves would cost a thousand honest histories.
